overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics shows a clear dominance of extreme space phenomenons, esoteric planetary conditions, and 'What If' hypothetical space scenarios. Specifically, videos covering rare planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond planets, planets darker than coal, burning ice planets) and extreme cosmic attributes are driving the highest views-per-day and stronger engagement rates (likes-per-view and comments-per-view). Conversely, older biological or psychological facts published earlier in September are seeing heavily diminished daily velocities.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views), and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) significantly outperform standard biological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal, high-scale space 'What If' scenarios and extreme exoplanet descriptions featuring rich visual cues.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) demonstrate strong pull via contradictory or impossible-sounding weather/physics.
winning_patterns.action: Utilize short, punchy titles featuring impossible physics or extreme weather on exotic celestial bodies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views depending on age) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) show severely flatlined daily views due to saturation.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks unless paired with a completely novel, cinematic mystery angle.

next_video.concept: What happens if you stood on a rogue planet hurtling through interstellar space with no star?
next_video.opening_direction: Start in absolute pitch blackness and absolute zero temperature, then reveal a terrifying rogue world wandering the void without a sun.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite having no star, the core is hot enough to maintain massive subterranean oceans of liquid nitrogen or boiling neon.
next_video.reason: Rogue planets and interstellar anomalies tap directly into the top-performing space 'What If' sub-niche identified in recent metrics.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond planets, TrES-2b, or Saturn comparisons
Must use a completely new celestial entity or astronomical phenomenon not present in historical data

experiment: Test a 21-second narrative structure with an immediate sensory shock hook ('Your blood would boil and freeze simultaneously...') applied to a rogue interstellar planet concept to benchmark retention against standard space factoids.
